newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: Plessey sells cellular stake to black group.
newsitem.headline: Plessey sells cellular stake to black group.

text.p: South African telecommunications company Plessey Corp Ltd said on Thursday it had sold 15 percent of its cellular service provider for 5.5 million rand in a black empowerment deal.
Plessey said it had sold the stake in Plessey Cellular, formerly known as Astec, to Brimstone Investment Ltd, a Western Cape-based grouping of black professionals and businessmen.
John Temple, Plessey's chief executive, said the company was keen to involve all sectors of the South African population in its business.
Earlier this year black investment company Worldwide Africa Investment Holdings increased its stake in Plessey to 26 percent from five, giving it joint control of the firm with Sankorp.
